item.title: In 1952, one of England’s rarest moths was last recorded at a Northumberland estate
item.description: Conservationists have triumphantly rediscovered a rare moth population that had been missing for seventy years at the National Trust's Wallington Estate in Northumberland. Thanks to extensive habitat restoration efforts, this elusive species, once threatened by extinction in England, has made a hopeful return, inspiring optimism for uncovering other hidden insect populations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2022, bird flu caused an entire Sandwich tern colony in England to be abandoned
item.description: In an inspiring turn of events, Sandwich Terns have returned to Pagham Harbour in unprecedented numbers following a devastating bird flu outbreak. Thanks to dedicated habitat restoration and predator management efforts, conservationists have helped establish one of England's largest breeding colonies. The sight of flourishing chicks this breeding season, nourished by ample food resources, signals a promising recovery for seabird populations grappling with the aftermath of disease.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: For nearly a decade, a California town fought to seize its privately owned water utility
item.description: In a landmark decision, California's Supreme Court dismissed a town's claim regarding the use of eminent domain for utility purposes. The judges emphasized the need for a thorough, independent evaluation of necessity declarations before any utility can be seized. This shift significantly impacts how courts will weigh municipal efforts to take over private utility companies, allowing private water, gas, and electricity firms to challenge such actions more effectively.

item.title: Chantelle Van Vliet wins £32,237 after being fired over menopause symptoms, tribunal rules
item.description: A 48-year-old beauty therapist was fired after requesting flexible working hours to manage severe menopause symptoms, including fatigue, confusion and brain fog. An employment tribunal found that she had been subjected to disability discrimination and denied reasonable workplace support. Chantelle Van Vliet was awarded £32,237 in compensation, although receiving the money remains uncertain because the company is in voluntary liquidation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Meet Alyssa Yu, the 17-year-old Maryland student who built a mathematical model for what...
item.description: A student from Maryland has developed an innovative model aimed at predicting the interactions of infectious diseases, effectively filling a critical gap in public health forecasting amid multiple outbreaks. Her groundbreaking research has garnered her recognition as a finalist in a national science competition. This mathematical framework could revolutionize the planning of focused vaccination campaigns during epidemics, providing essential strategies for managing disease transmission.

item.title: Meet Kinley Rasmus, the 12-year-old Alabama girl who became only the 25th girl to play in the...
item.description: Kinley Rasmus made history as the 25th girl to participate in the Little League World Series. With a remarkable debut, she pitched six scoreless innings, striking out eight batters, equaling Mo'ne Davis's record for female pitchers. Additionally, Rasmus made her mark by setting a record for the highest number of hits by a female player, earning admiration from fans across the nation.

item.title: Meet Ashka Shah, the 17-year-old New York student who studied how a cancer-driving protein
item.description: A student from New York has pioneered a groundbreaking technique aimed at halting the growth of cancer cells. This research focuses on a crucial protein linked to the rapid development of tumors. By inhibiting the harmful activity of this protein, her method preserves the viability of healthy cells. She gained national acclaim as a finalist in a prestigious science competition, illuminating a promising new pathway for precision cancer therapies.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US colleges are rolling out three-year bachelor's degrees in 120 programmes across 26 states
item.description: US colleges are increasingly offering three-year bachelor's degree programmes that require 90 credits instead of the traditional 120. The programmes are now available or announced in 26 states, with 119 reduced-credit programmes identified by RAND. Supporters say they can save students time and money, while critics question their impact on learning, professional licensing, graduate admissions and employer acceptance.

item.title: Holly Madison won’t sell her ‘haunted’ LA home; lists it for rent at $9,500 a month
item.description: Holly Madison has listed her historic Tudor-style Los Angeles home for $9,500 a month after deciding not to sell it. She bought the property for just under $1.5 million in 2012 and has described it as a fairytale-like home. The house was also investigated for paranormal activity in 2021. Madison says she may eventually keep the property for retirement and pass it on to her children.

item.title: Singapore is paying parents $55,000 to have babies; here's why
item.description: In a groundbreaking move, Singapore is launching a substantial financial support package designed for families with children. Targeted at reversing the alarming trend of declining birth rates, the government will provide up to S$70,000 per child until they reach seventeen. This initiative replaces previous schemes, providing consistent financial relief to parents, thereby encouraging family growth in the nation.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Michigan puts $6.5 million toward 22,650 Keweenaw acres as conservation fund tops $1.4 billion
item.description: Michigan’s Natural Resources Trust Fund is marking 50 years of supporting land conservation and outdoor recreation. Created in 1976 using earnings from state-owned oil, gas and mineral revenues, the fund has awarded nearly $1.4 billion so far. Its latest grants include $6.5 million to acquire nearly 22,650 acres in the Keweenaw Peninsula, along with funding for parks, trails, waterfront areas and recreation projects across Michigan.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A New Zealand sailor spent years living alone on a remote Cook Islands atoll across 3 separate stays
item.description: Suwarrow atoll, once the secluded refuge of hermit Tom Neale, has transformed into the Cook Islands' inaugural conservation sanctuary. After Neale spent sixteen years in seclusion on Anchorage Island, the atoll was designated as a national park and bird haven. This vital area now protects critical seabird nesting grounds and marine ecosystems, allowing Neale's legacy to be honored through his preserved hut and a tribute on the island.
